_comment: Copy this file to metrics.json to put a metric glossary in force.
No glossary ships with the repository: certifying a metric is a
statement that an organisation agrees on a definition and that a named
person owns it, and a default owner would be a fabricated one.
Runs without a glossary say plainly that their measure is undefined.
Each entry: name, a definition in words, the columns the metric may
appear as, and optionally a formula. Certified entries must name an
owner — certification with nobody accountable is a rubber stamp.
A formula is one operation over column names: sum, multiply (two or
more columns), subtract or divide (exactly two). Where the formula's
columns are present, every row is checked against it and rows that do
not match are reported. That is the difference between a glossary and
a document: this one can be wrong out loud.

metrics.name: revenue
metrics.title: Net Revenue
metrics.definition: Invoiced amount after discounts, excluding tax and shipping.

metrics.name: gross_margin
metrics.title: Gross Margin
metrics.definition: Net revenue less cost of goods sold, before operating costs.

metrics.name: average_order_value
metrics.title: Average Order Value
metrics.definition: Net revenue divided by the number of completed orders. Cancelled orders are excluded from both parts.
